task: Write one sentence of your own using the word tranquil. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know tranquil should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The valley is at its most tranquil under new snow, every sound wrapped in white.
Peaceful is milder and broader than tranquil—a peaceful afternoon may still hold lawnmowers and laughter, while a tranquil one has settled into a real, unbroken hush.
Still goes further than peaceful or tranquil—stillness is the total pause, not a leaf turning, while a tranquil scene may yet ripple softly at its edges.

Restful means the place actively restores you—an hour there and you leave better, the way sleep works. Tranquil describes the scene's own undisturbed state, whether or not it restores anyone: a tranquil ruin can be melancholy. Restful is about what the calm does for you; tranquil is about the calm itself.

Quiet is a report about sound and nothing else—the room is not noisy just now. Tranquil promises more: that nothing is wrong beneath the hush, no hurry, no trouble waiting. A hospital corridor at three a.m. is quiet; a harbor at dusk is tranquil.

It promises freedom from disturbance—quieter than 'peaceful' and more outward than serene, which lives behind a person's eyes.
